minutes.headline: Budget Task Force reviewed town and school revenue data and flagged investment income and a vanished revenue line to pursue.
minutes.summary: The task force heard a master revenue presentation covering state aid versus tax levy, local receipts, fees, new growth and comparison towns, followed by school-side revenue streams. Members focused on poorly invested town accounts, an unexplained drop in a miscellaneous non-recurring line, and Medicaid reimbursement. No formal votes were recorded; the next meeting will look at expenses and the treasurer may be invited.

public_comment.topic: Mr pasos was invited first; the captions do not make clear what he said, and an observer said he was only there to observe.

Dave pasio (56 wedding Street) praised the task force, said the CPA attempt never got past the select board, urged contacting the library trustees about raising investment returns, and proposed seeking a state empowerment act for a local income tax.

budget_items.what_was_said: Presenter observed an inverse relationship between tax levy and state aid shares across towns. Another member said this is the expected net effect of the state formulas, not causal.
This local receipts line dropped sharply around FY16 and stayed down, and nobody knows what it contained. Carter will dig through records.
Revenue from the fees line rose over five years, more steadily than in other towns.
Reimbursement program for DPW road work, funds accumulate and stay available; a plan was presented to the selectboard.
First funded in FY24, restricted to roads and bridges, in addition to Chapter 90. School-related portion covers free lunches; schools not eligible for a grant.
Town-side line dropped away; school-based Medicaid is a school claim and is believed to bring in a steady amount, but where it is recorded is unclear.
Town earns little compared with peers, with many accounts at very low rates and millions sitting idle. Consolidation and better returns were called a quick win.
A member estimated that restoring the vanished revenue streams and fixing investments could find a large sum.
CPA would add a surcharge with a partial state match, restricted to open space, recreation and housing, not operating revenue.

budget_items.topic: School revenue streams: Chapter 70, circuit breaker, grants
budget_items.what_was_said: Chapter 70 is steadily increasing; circuit breaker reimburses a share of high-need special education; entitlement and competitive grants described.
Tuition is variable and depends on committee decisions; the committee chose not to expand slots, so no increase is projected.
Fees have not risen in six years while costs have, and fees do not cover athletics costs. Fee relief tied to lunch status and sibling discounts.
Cell tower rent goes to the town, possibly the turf revolving account or the fees line, not through the school district.
School side is trying to untangle solar agreements and credit rates; buying out leases was suggested.

decisions.decision: Invite the treasurer to a task force meeting to discuss investment strategy and the FY24 figures.
Raise a review of trust fund and investment accounts with the finance team this week, possibly asking Bartholomew.
A member will contact an expert on another board for names of people who can advise on investment consolidation.
Next meeting will look at expenses, focusing on unavoidable contractual and statutory costs, and try to identify the miscellaneous non-recurring revenue.
Next meeting set for two weeks out, the 29th.
Town will ask the assessor to preview the classification hearing material and make it more informative.

what_happened.line: The Budget Task Force heard a master presentation on town revenue, then school revenue streams, and recorded no formal votes.
Members flagged town investment income as a possible quick win, citing many accounts at very low rates and idle balances.
A local receipts line for miscellaneous non-recurring revenue dropped sharply around FY16 and stayed down; nobody present knew what it held, and Carter will search records.
The task force agreed to invite the treasurer to discuss investment strategy and the FY24 figures.
The next meeting, set for the 29th, will look at expenses, mainly contractual and statutory costs, and try to identify the vanished revenue line.

why_it_matters: Interest earned on town cash and trust accounts, and any revenue line that disappeared, can reduce how much must be raised through the tax levy, so these are the places the task force is looking for money before asking residents for more.
The school-side discussion showed that state aid and fees, not the levy alone, carry much of the school budget, and athletics fees have stayed flat while costs rose.
